Article Title: Vishwakarma Puja: The Day Nobody Touched the Tools
Article Text:
Idols of Lord Vishwakarma are on display for sale in Kolkata

Kites being bought

Bhadre rendhe, Ashwine khaoa

Sources/Reading:

Dipesh Chakrabarty, Rethinking Working-Class History: Bengal 1890–1940 (Princeton University Press, 1989)

Leela Fernandes, Producing Workers: The Politics of Gender, Class, and Culture in the Calcutta Jute Mills (University of Pennsylvania Press, 1997)

On Vishwakarma Puja, remembering a leather factory that honoured a Hindu god with Muslim hands participating and biryani from Park Street. Nobody thought it needed explaining.Few Hindu festivals can be entered in an office calendar years ahead without consulting a panjika, and Vishwakarma Puja, which falls today, is the most dependable of them, because it is pegged to Kanya Sankranti, the last day of Bhadra, a solar date rather than a lunar one, which is why it generally lands on September 17 every year.It seems only right that the god of engineers should keep better time than most gods.He is, by his résumé, the most accomplished contractor in the Hindu universe. Tradition credits him with Lord Krishna's Dwarka, the golden Lanka that Hanuman ji later set alight, the Pandava capital at Indraprastha and the chariots in which the gods flew. What is less remarked upon is how differently India has chosen to picture him. In the west and north-west he is an old, four-armed man with a white beard and a swan for a mount, which scholars read as a nod to Brahma; in the east he is a young, muscular man with a black moustache, no sons in attendance, and an elephant as his vahana, which suggests God Indra instead.West Bengal, a state with no shortage of bearded elders, decided that its engineer should look like a foreman in his prime, which tells you something about who was doing the worshipping.The flying chariots are how Bengal explains its kites, which dot Kolkata's skies on this day. Hindu mythology is full of gods travelling by air, and Vishwakarma is held to have built the vehicles. The skies over Kolkata on this day used to (and perhaps still do to a lesser extent) fill with petkati and chandiyal, and the morning began with the cry of bhokatta from some rooftop where a boy had just cut a rival's string.Held on the last day of Bhadra, the puja also opens the long Sharodiya season, so the kites were, in effect, the city's first announcement that Maa Durga was on her way. In many Bengali homes the day carries a second observance that has nothing to do with machines. Arandhan, tied to Manasa Puja at Bhadra Sankranti, requires that food be cooked the night before and eaten stale the next day, with cooking itself forbidden; the custom has loosened with modern life but survives in Bengal's villages and in Kolkata's suburbs. The folk phrase for it,— cook in Bhadra and eat in Ashwin — is as good a summary as any.The puja's real home, though, was never the household. It is observed mostly on factory floors, where workers pray for safe conditions and for their machines to run well, and shrines go up among the tools themselves. Historians studying Kolkata's working class have argued that this was something the workers made their own; Dipesh Chakrabarty wrote about festivals as a source of solidarity inside hostile workplaces, and Leela Fernandes's ethnography of the jute mills treated the building of Vishwakarma pandals as a space of the workers' cultural autonomy.The leather factory: My family's business was a leather factory on Tiljala Road, right behind Don Bosco School, and on this day the more than four hundred men who worked there, nearly all of them Muslim, did not touch their tools. The work that honoured the god had been done the day before, when the craftsmen who spent the rest of the year shaping leather goods turned to sheets of coloured paper instead, cutting out decorations with a skill that matched their day jobs and a gusto that suggested they found paper the more forgiving material. Everything the day required was prepared on the eve, and on the day itself the hands rested.By the time the priest arrived, the god of craftsmen was presiding over a room that craftsmen, most of whom did not pray to him, had dressed for him. I have never been sure how much of the abstention was reverence and how much was the ordinary pleasure of a working day on which no work was expected, and I suspect the men themselves would have found the question tiresome, which is perhaps the point.Then there was lunch. Many factory feasts on the day were vegetarian, a mutton curry being the mark of the more generous units, and ours had apparently decided that gastronomy in this feast was a competitive sport and opted for biryani. The biryani came from Shiraz on Park Street, which opened in 1941 at the Park Street and Mullick Bazar crossing, specialising in Awadhi food, founded by Mohammed Arshad Ali and Ali Hussain, who had come to Calcutta from Bihar. Calcutta's biryani, as every Calcuttan will tell you at length, came down from Awadh with Wajid Ali Shah's exile, and Shiraz's cook Shamsuddin, who joined in the 1970s and reworked its biryani, is said to have had an ancestor who cooked for the nawab.Consider the arrangement then. A feast for the Hindu god of craft, cooked to a deposed Muslim king's recipe by a kitchen that claims descent from his, eaten by four hundred Muslim leatherworkers and one Bengali Hindu family, on a day when the stoves in half of Bengal's kitchens were not supposed to be lit. The factory had solved Arandhan by outsourcing it to a Park Street restaurant, and nobody, as far as I remember, felt the need to hold a seminar about it. (We'd hold a good many seminars or news channel debates now.)The next morning the god went into the waters of the Hooghly, and the men went back to their benches. The tools, having been worshipped for a day, went back to being worked, which is, if you think about it, the only form of worship a tool has ever asked for.
Article Summary: Vishwakarma puja falls on kanya sankranti, the last day of bhadra. The skies over kolkata used to fill with petkati and chandiyal. It is observed mostly on factory floors. The hindu festival of arandhan took place in kolkata in the 1950s. The festival was a time of rest and celebration for the city's working class.

Article Title: Graham Staines case: SC asks Dara Singh to tweak remission plea for relief hearing
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Thursday granted two weeks to murder convict Dara Singh to challenge the Odisha government's decision rejecting his plea for premature release in the 1999 murder case of Australian missionary Graham Staines and his two minor sons.The top court's decision comes days after the Odisha government pointed out the gravity of the offence and said Singh's plea for premature release had been rejected after considering all facts and circumstances of the case.The top court agreed to hear Singh's petition after three weeks.

Australian missionary graham staines and his two minor sons were murdered in 1999. The top court agreed to hear singh's petition after three weeks.

Article Title: E-waste from govt offices may fetch Rs 10,000 cr a year: MoS Jitendra Singh
Article Text:
Union MoS Jitendra Singh speaks during the launch of the Special Campaign 6 Monitoring portal to track the implementation of the campaign aimed at institutionalising Swachhata and reducing pendency across government offices, in New Delhi. (Photo: ANI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Launching the dedicated web-portal for the sixth edition of govt’s ‘special campaign’ to declutter govt offices, minister of state for personnel Jitendra Singh on Wednesday said the focus will henceforth shift to responsible disposal of non-functional electronic items lying in govt offices, with annual earnings from e-waste recycling expected to touch Rs 10,000 crore in a few years.According to secretary, ministry of mines, Keshav Chandra, e-waste has become the most valuable commodity as an input for the industry. E waste, when crushed together, generates ‘black mass’, which contains 30% of critical mineral requirements. This is the reason why most advanced economies of the world have the export of black mass. “Instead of going outside seeking critical minerals, we can obtain them from e-waste recycling,” Chandra said, adding that ‘Special Campaign 6’ will serve the dual purpose of removing garbage from govt offices and obtaining value from it.The ‘special campaign’ initiative to free up space and institutionalise cleanliness across govt offices was launched in 2021 and runs each year between the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi’s on Oct 2 to that of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel on Oct 31. Over the years, the swachata initiative and special campaign have helped free up over 1,000 lakh square feet of office space, led to weeding out or closure of around 2 crore files and generated a revenue of Rs 5,103 crore from scrap disposal.“These achievements reflect the expansion of swachhata campaign beyond cleanliness to efficient utilisation of govt resources, reduction of pendency, better use of public spaces and conversion of waste into wealth,” Singh said while addressing mediapersons at the launch of Special Campaign 6.Secretary for the department of administrative reforms and public grievances (DARPG) Nivedita Shukla Verma said the govt will ensure that e-waste collected during the special campaign is handed over only to registered recyclers and disposed of in an environmentally sound manner.As many as 58 big recyclers have already registered to process the e-waste, according to Chandra.The govt had last year run a limited campaign for e-waste collection across 58 locations, placing bins in govt offices to collect non-functional and unused computers, keyboards, printers, laptops etc. The response encouraged the govt to make e-waste collection and recycling a critical component of Special Campaign 6.
Article Summary: The focus will henceforth shift to responsible disposal of non-functional electronic items lying in govt offices. Annual earnings from e-waste recycling expected to touch rs 10,000 crore in a few years. E waste, when crushed together, generates ‘black mass’, which contains 30% of critical mineral requirements.

Article Title: CBI files FIR in Disha Salian's death case after HC order
Article Text:
The court had criticised the Mumbai Police for failing to register an FIR despite the investigation continuing for nearly six years

Aaditya Thackeray, Rhea Chakraborty & Dino Morea named In CBI FIR

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: CBI has filed an FIR and formed a special team to probe the death of Disha Salian, two weeks after Bombay HC ordered it to take over the case. The FIR has been filed under IPC sections covering offences such as gang rape, murder and destruction of evidence, etc.No one has been named as an accused in the case. But the FIR content, based on a complaint by Disha's father Satish Salian, mentions several people, including Aditya Thackeray, Dino Morea and Rhea Chakraborty, saying their roles need to be probed.Disha, who worked as actor Sushant Singh Rajput's manager, was found dead on June 8, 2020, after falling from the 14th floor of a residential building in Mumbai. A week later, Sushant was found dead at his Bandra flat.Satish Salian recorded his statement before CBI last week, and it was converted into the FIR on Sept 13.The FIR alleges that the then chief minister, Uddhav Thackeray, father of Aaditya, and others also played a significant role in an alleged conspiracy and the subsequent cover-up.It also alleges that some public servants and police officers need to be investigated for destruction or suppression of case papers, files and other public records, fabrication of official records, and misuse of public funds, manpower and police machinery for unlawful purposes and for shielding the offenders.The FIR claims: "The persons whose roles require investigation in connection with the commission of the principal offences, criminal conspiracy, subsequent creation and propagation of the false suicide story, and suppression, destruction and/or fabrication of evidence include Aaditya Thackeray, Rohan Roy, Dino Morea, Sooraj Pancholi, Aaditya Thackeray's bodyguards, Rhea Chakraborty, Showik Chakraborty, Sachin Vaze, Param Bir Singh, DCP Vishal Thakur, Uddhav Thackeray, Anil Deshmukh, API Ashok Devadhe, PI Jagdev Kalapad, PI Shailendra Nagarkar, PI Chimaji Adhav, PI Arjun Rajane, concerned officers of Malvani Police Station".It also calls for the questioning of the autopsy and forensic officials besides several others, including the building's security guards.
Article Summary: Cbi has filed an fir and formed a special team to probe the death of disha salian. Bombay hc ordered it to take over the case two weeks ago. Disha, who worked as actor sushant singh rajput's manager, was found dead in 2020.

Article Title: ‘Umar Khalid is a nationalist’: B K Hariprasad’s remark sparks BJP attack
Article Text:
Karnataka Congress president B K Hariprasad called jailed activist Umar Khalid a nationalist.





BENGALURU: Karnataka Congress president B K Hariprasad Tuesday called jailed activist Umar Khalid a “nationalist” and criticised Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad ( ABVP ) for opposing a proposed screening of a documentary on him at National Law School of India University (NLSIU).“ABVP has no right to speak about Khalid because ABVP adores Nathuram Godse, who is anti-national and the first terrorist of the country,” Hariprasad said.The remarks came after ABVP in Bengaluru demanded cancellation of the proposed screening of filmmaker Lalit Vachani’s documentary, ‘Prisoner No. 626710 is Present’, at NLSIU. The documentary was scheduled to be screened Monday by the law and society committee, a student organisation at the university. NLSIU later said it had to reschedule the event due to “logistical and security considerations”.The screening was to express solidarity with Khalid and to mark six years since his imprisonment without trial under Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act in connection with the 2020 Delhi riots.BJP hit back at Hariprasad’s remarks, calling them deeply condemnable. In New Delhi, Sambit Patra, MP, linked Hariprasad’s remarks to Congress’ past interactions with Kashmiri separatist leader Yasin Malik.“Just think about it: this is the same Umar Khalid,” Patra said. “During the Citizenship Amendment Act protests in Feb 2020, so many people were killed in Delhi. A case was filed under UAPA. The matter was heard across multiple courts; even in Feb 2026, the Supreme Court rejected Umar Khalid’s bail plea. Look at the sympathy Congress party harbours for the very same Umar Khalid.”Patra also attacked Congress party over its meetings with Yasin Malik, alleging the party had reduced itself to “appeasement”.
Article Summary: Karnataka congress president b k hariprasad called jailed activist umar khalid a nationalist. He criticised akhil bharatiya vidyarthi parishad ( abvp ) for opposing a proposed screening of a documentary on him at national law school of india university.

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay's public event outside London's iconic Shard skyscraper was cancelled after the Metropolitan Police raised concerns over crowd safety.Hundreds of fans had gathered at the venue, with several waiting for hours to see the actor-turned-politician. Vijay's team announced the cancellation over a loudspeaker, citing the lack of police permission on safety grounds.“For public safety concerns, we are calling off the programme because we don't have permission due to safety concerns,” a member of the chief minister's team said.Hours after the cancellation of the event, TVK's IT wing said in a social media post on X urged fans to refrain from waiting at the entrance of the hotel or making any attempts to meet him."We would be filled with love and heartfelt enthusiasm to meet the Tamil Nadu chief minister Thiru C Joseph Vijay. However, keeping the safety of the public in mind and considering the request of the London Metropolitan Police, an unavoidable situation has arisen where the chief minister and victorious leader cannot meet with you. Therefore, with affection, we kindly request that no one attempt to meet him," TVK's IT wing said."Furthermore, with humility, we request that you refrain from efforts such as waiting at the entrance of the hotel where the victorious leader is staying or along the route he will travel," it added.Vijay is in the UK as part of a state delegation seeking investments for Tamil Nadu. His office said earlier that the delegation had signed multiple memoranda of understanding involving investments worth around Rs 12,300 crore during the visit.The investment agreements are part of the state's effort to position Tamil Nadu as a leading advanced manufacturing and technology hub in Asia. The projects are expected to create more than 9,400 high-value jobs across the state.Vijay is scheduled to conclude his UK visit and return to India on Wednesday.

Article Title: Maratha activist Jarange Patil calls off 20-day fast, gives govt 3 months to consider demands
Article Text:
Jarange said it was not possible to continue a rally tour while observing an indefinite hunger strike.

NEW DELHI: Maratha reservation activist Manoj Jarange Patil on Thursday called off his 20-day-old hunger strike and gave the Maharashtra government three months to consider his demands, news agency PTI reported.The decision came after Jarange addressed a large gathering at Patoda in Beed district around 2 am, raising concerns about his worsening physical condition and the possibility of abandoning his planned march to Mumbai.Jarange, who had entered the day 18 of his fast at the time of the address, said he was too physically exhausted to continue a long journey with thousands of supporters travelling behind him.He asked Maratha community members not to follow his vehicle after he left Patoda. Instead, he urged them to meet him directly at Khopoli. He warned that if the convoy continued, he might stop the journey and resume his sit-in protest in Patoda or return to Antarwali Sarati.Despite reaching the venue at around 1.30 am, Jarange found thousands of people, including women, waiting to hear him speak.Addressing the gathering, he said he could barely move his limbs after stopping IV fluids on September 12."Fighting for the children of my community has taken a toll on my body, but I have taken on the government for you. The government wants me to surrender, but should I abandon our demand? My community is greater than any government - it is my father. My community holds the power to bring down any government and install a new one," he asserted.Jarange said the movement had made progress after 58 lakh archival records, known as nondi, were uncovered. He claimed these records could help nearly 2.5 crore members of the Maratha community access reservation benefits.He said the immediate demand was for the Maharashtra government to issue an official gazette recognising the relevant records.The activist also criticised chief minister Devendra Fadnavis, claiming he had countered the government's political moves and that all the documented records had been secured on pen drives. He further accused Fadnavis of "plotting against his life".Responding to the government's argument about fruit orchard owners in Western Maharashtra, Jarange questioned why OBC communities that also own orchards should not receive reservation benefits."The government claims Western Maharashtra has fruit orchards, but don't OBC communities own orchards too? Why do they have a reservation then?"Jarange said it was not possible to continue a rally tour while observing an indefinite hunger strike. He appealed to supporters to avoid following his vehicle and said he would prefer to travel directly to Mumbai from Patoda after speaking to the police, if his health allowed.He also spoke about his family, saying he had asked them to live with self-respect and told his son to remain courageous if he died for the community."I have told my family to live with self-respect. I told my son to step up courageously if I give my life for the community. Let one life be sacrificed for the cause, but never let the dignity of our caste be lowered," he said.
Article Summary: Jarange said it was not possible to continue a rally tour while observing an indefinite hunger strike. He asked maratha community members not to follow his vehicle after he left patoda. Instead, he urged them to meet him directly at khopoli.

Article Title: 'Perfect in doing drama': SC gives Rajpal Yadav final chance to deposit Rs 2 crore
Article Text:
'Perfect in doing drama': SC gives Rajpal Yadav final chance to deposit Rs 2 crore

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Tuesday gave Bollywood actor Rajpal Yadav a final opportunity to deposit at least Rs 2 crore with the Supreme Court Registry within two weeks in connection with a cheque bounce case involving a private complainant.Rajpal is accused of owing Rs 5 crore to the owner of Murali Productions.Also read | Rajpal gets interim relief in cheque bounce case, SC exempts surrender if he deposits Rs 5 cr by Wednesday A bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant noted that the actor's past conduct in the matter did not inspire confidence.However, the top court granted him two weeks after his counsel assured the bench that Rajpal would deposit at least Rs 2 crore within the deadline and provide a surety for the remaining amount.“Looking at his past conduct.. how can anybody trust him? Article Title: Aaditya Thackeray, Rhea Chakraborty named in Disha Salian's death case: Key details from CBI FIR
Article Text:
Earlier, the Bombay HC ordered a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into Salian's death.

Bombay HC orders CBI probe

NEW DELHI: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) on Monday registered an FIR in connection with the death of Disha Salian, the former manager of late actor Sushant Singh Rajput, following an order of the Bombay high court.No one has been named as an accused in the case. However, the FIR, based on a complaint filed by Disha’s father, Satish Salian, names several people whose alleged roles have been listed for investigation.The FIR names several individuals whose roles have been listed for investigation, including Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Aaditya Thackeray, Rohan Roy, actors Dino Morea and Sooraj Pancholi, Aaditya's bodyguards, Rhea Chakraborty , Showik Chakraborty, former police officer Sachin Vaze, former Mumbai police commissioner Param Bir Singh, DCP Vishal Thakur and former Maharashtra chief minister Uddhav Thackeray.The document also names former state home minister Anil Deshmukh, several police officers, forensic officials, doctors and other individuals.“The then chief minister Uddhav Thackeray, father of Aaditya Thackeray, and others also played a significant role in the conspiracy and subsequent cover-up. The concerned public servants and police officers are also liable to be investigated for destruction or suppression of case papers, files and other public records, fabrication of official records, and misuse of public funds, manpower and police machinery for unlawful purposes and for shielding the offenders,” the FIR stated.The FIR said the listed individuals would be investigated in connection with the alleged principal offences, criminal conspiracy, the “subsequent creation and propagation of the false suicide story” and the alleged suppression, destruction or fabrication of evidence.It also named officers associated with Malvani Police Station, doctors and staff involved in the post-mortem, officials of the Forensic Science Laboratory in Kalina, security guards of Regent Galaxy Building, members of the special investigation team and other unidentified persons.Earlier this month, the Bombay high court ordered a CBI investigation into Salian’s death and criticised the Mumbai Police for failing to register an FIR for six years.The court observed that the police investigation “raises more questions than answers”. The bench also questioned the decision to treat the case only as an accidental death and pointed to “glaring discrepancies” in the investigation.Salian died on June 8, 2020, after falling from a residential building in Mumbai’s Malad area. Mumbai Police had registered an Accidental Death Report (ADR) in the case.Salian had briefly worked as Sushant's manager. The actor was found dead at his Bandra residence on June 14, 2020, six days after Salian’s death.The proximity of the two deaths triggered widespread speculation about a possible link, although the cases were investigated separately.Following the public uproar over Rajput’s death, the Maharashtra government ordered a CBI probe. The agency later submitted a closure report stating that Rajput had died by suicide. The report, however, is yet to be heard by the court concerned.Earlier, Salian’s father, Satish Salian, had accused Aaditya Thackeray and actor Dino Morea in connection with his daughter’s death.Speaking to ANI on Friday, Satish Salian said he had told investigators what he knew about the events surrounding his daughter's death and provided names of several individuals whom he wanted authorities to examine.“I stated the facts exactly as they were; I told them everything that happened to my daughter. I listed all the names: Aditya, Sooraj Pancholi, Dino Morea, and the bodyguards. They noted everything down. They said they would take action based on what I told them; the proceedings would begin in a few days,” he said.“The truth cannot be defeated. God stands where the truth is; that is why justice will be served,” he added. Mumbai Police had earlier maintained, after its inquiry, that Salian had died by suicide.
Article Summary: The central bureau of investigation (cbi) on monday registered an fir in connection with the death of disha salian, the former manager of late actor sushant singh rajput. No one has been named as an accused in the case. However, the fir, based on a complaint filed by disha’s father, satish salian.

Article Title: SC pulls up govt for 'denying' disabled soldiers their benefits
Article Text:
SC junked over 270 appeals filed by govt against such soldiers

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Quoting Raksha Mantri 2015 Report, which admitted that "many disabled soldiers in India are still denied disability benefits on hyper-technical reasons", Supreme Court has pulled up Centre and the defence ministry for litigating against them in all forums of the judiciary - from tribunals to HCs and SC. It also highlighted that govt filed appeals after a long time in most of the cases.A bench of Justices P S Narasimha and Alok Aradhe noted that Raksha Mantri Report had recommended the immediate withdrawal of appeals pertaining to disability and pensionary benefits pending against soldiers with disabilities but said the recommendation had not been faithfully implemented. "Appeals such as these are filed and continue to be filed, even after the ministry of defence accepted the committee's recommendation for withdrawal of this class of litigation," the bench said, junking over 270 appeals filed by govt.The bench also examined the outcome of such cases in different judicial forums."The sad part of this litigation is that, out of around 271 civil appeals and special leave petitions, most of them are barred by limitation. Many similar appeals that were barred by limitation have already been dismissed in the past; the present batch is only a small number that survive. Moreover, it is significant to note that the number of appeals rejected at the first appellate stage, after a dismissal by the release medical board, far exceeds those accepted," SC said.According to information obtained under RTI Act, of the 2,997 appeals before the first appellate authority, 2,855 were rejected and only 142 appeals were accepted, the bench added. Before the second appellate authority, out of 456 appeals, 439 were rejected and only 17 accepted.The court examined Entitlement Rules 2008, passed in 2010 to replace the 1982 rules, and did not find any error in them. The 1982 Rules clearly create a presumption that if a member of the service is in sound physical and mental health at the time of entrance, then any disability at the time of discharge would be attributable to military service. The 2008 Rules, however, withdraw this presumption by adding a causal connection requirement. They say, "Mere fact that a disease has manifested during military service does not per se establish attributability to or aggravation by military service."The bench upheld the new rules, saying, "The mere addition of a causal requirement and a removal of the presumption that when a member joins service healthy, and, if, he leaves with a disability, it ought to be attributable to the military service, does not, by itself, change the core scheme of the Entitlement Rules 2008 because the other beneficial provisions broadly remain untouched. The onus to prove that the member's disability is not attributable to service still lies on the employer. The relevant rules regarding attributability and aggravation continue to hold that if cause of disability is unknown,... then the disability is attributable to service."
Article Summary: Sc junked over 270 appeals filed by govt against such soldiers. Supreme court has pulled up centre and the defence ministry for litigating against them. It also highlighted that govt filed appeals after a long time in most of the cases.

Article Title: OBC creamy layer: In a knot, govt tries to untie itself before SC, CAT
Article Text:
After petitioning SC on Aug 25 raising questions about the judgement, govt has now asked CAT to modify its Aug 19 order

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Centre has begun to disentangle itself from the seemingly contradictory positions it has taken before Supreme Court and Central Administrative Tribunal on the implementation of the March 11 Rohit Nathan judgement on creamy layer for OBCs from PSU family background.Rohit Nathan judgement paved way for the induction of those OBC candidates in the elite civil services who passed exams over past 10 years but were still left out. The judgement laid down that "salary" cannot be added to "income" to decide if a candidate from PSU background falls in "creamy layer" - like it is done for OBCs from non-PSU families.After petitioning SC on Aug 25 raising questions about the judgement, govt has now asked CAT to modify its Aug 19 order where Centre had committed to implement the Nathan judgement.In an affidavit filed in CAT Monday, govt said its earlier submission "that a decision has been taken to implement the judgement in Rohit Nathan requires to be suitably clarified" because a modification application is pending before SC. Govt said the judgement's implementation would depend on the outcome of pending application in SC.Govt has told CAT that if its earlier order stays on record in its unqualified form, "it is likely to create an inconsistent position" suggesting govt has undertaken to implement the judgement that it has assailed before SC.TOI had reported how Centre has taken a contradictory stand before SC and CAT in the wake of OBC candidate Basant Singh pushing the tribunal to enforce its order that he be inducted in civil services. Singh's case is similar to the candidates in whose favour SC delivered the Nathan judgement. Quoting the fresh affidavit, Vikram Hegde, lawyer for Singh, said, " Govt is seeking to set the clock back."As per the 1993 office memorandum, "salary" and "agricultural income" are not included in computing "income" of a family. The case pertains to how DoPT has been taking "salary" into consideration for candidates with parents in PSUs.
Article Summary: After petitioning sc on aug 25 raising questions about the judgement, govt has now asked cat to modify its aug 19 order where centre had committed to implement the nathan judgement. Govt said the judgement's implementation would depend on the outcome of pending application in sc.

NEW DELHI: Unhappy with a Jodhpur labour court award, a health worker from Jalore district, Rajasthan, engaged on a daily wage basis and whose services were terminated in 1999 had moved Rajasthan HC in 2004.The petition is yet to be heard, 22 years later.With pendency in HCs crossing the 65 lakh mark, there is a steady stream of petitions before the Supreme Court pleading for directions to the HCs concerned, not for expeditious adjudication of their grievance but for early hearing on their petitions after prolonged wait for justice. Nearly 15 lakh such cases have remained pending in HCs for over a a decade.Most applications come from Allahabad HC and Rajasthan HC, where the pendency of cases is 12.5 lakh and 7 lakh respectively.In Allahabad HC, each judge/bench takes up an average of 150-200 cases every day for hearing, but the monstrous pendency appears to be overwhelming the judicial decision-making capacity. The erstwhile health worker from Jalore made a similar plea before a bench headed by CJI Surya Kant Wednesday.Given the constitutionally independent status of HCs and realising the daily case list before each judge in HCs, the CJI-led bench passed the standard order, "We see no ground to entertain the petition but give liberty to the petitioner to move an application seeking early hearing of the petition."The SC is aware that it is not superior to HCs on the administrative side and the chief justices concerned of HCs, as per the SC's own ruling, are the masters of roster, prohibiting it from directing them to list certain cases for early hearing.Moreover, if the SC requests an HC to hear one case out of turn considering the number of years for which it had remained pending, then the scale of equality would mandate early hearing of all similarly old petitions.After Allahabad and Rajasthan HCs, Bombay HC has the largest pendency of 6.4 lakh cases, followed by Madras HC with 5.6 lakh cases, Madhya Pradesh HC with 4.9 lakh, Karnataka HC with 3.3 lakh, and Andhra Pradesh HC with 2.5 lakh. Compared to Bombay and Madras HCs, the HCs of Delhi and Calcutta have relatively low pendency of cases at 1.2 lakh and 1.9 lakh cases.

Article Title: BIS raises gold hallmarking fee to Rs 75 per article
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Ahead of the festive season, Bureau of Indian Standards has raised with immediate effect the hallmarking charges for gold articles to Rs 75 from Rs 45 while retaining the charge for silver at Rs 35.As per the amended norm, jewellers are required to pay a hallmarking fee of Rs 75 per article, subject to a minimum charge of Rs 200 per consignment, while for silver articles, the fee payable by jewellers to recognised Assaying and Hallmarking Centres is fixed at Rs 35 per article, with a minimum of Rs 150 per consignment.BIS hallmarking verifies purity of precious metals.

Article Title: Good El Nino? How a bad monsoon left Delhi drenched
Article Text:
Delhi had a season’s rainfall surplus of 8% in a meteorological subdivision (Haryana)

Wet capital

NEW DELHI: The capital defied the odds this monsoon. As of Sept 16, Delhi had a season's rainfall surplus of 8% in a meteorological subdivision (Haryana) that's reeling under a 23% deficit and a region (northwest India) that has logged a 10% shortfall. The season's peculiar rainfall pattern indicates that a strengthening El Nino as well as climate change may have played a role in giving the capital an unlikely monsoon bounty.A look at the season's district-level rainfall map of the region shows Delhi literally at the edge of the good monsoon zone this year (see graphic). Just north of the capital lies a swathe of deficient districts starting with neighbouring Sonipat (-32%) and Rohtak (-47%) and all the way up to Hoshiarpur (-53%) and Kapurthala (-69%) in Punjab - a cluster of over 30 rain-starved districts in Haryana and Punjab as well as adjoining Rajasthan, Himachal and west UP.So how did Delhi turn into a wet pocket next to a rain-deficient region? The answer lies in the way low-pressure systems coming from Bay of Bengal shifted direction this season, probably under the influence of El Nino, and how their interactions with westerly disturbances uniquely aided rains in Delhi-NCR.A majority of monsoon rainfall in northwest and central India happens under the influence of moisture-laden low-pressure systems (LPSs), including depressions, travelling inland from Bay of Bengal.Contrary to what one would expect, the number of such systems does not decrease in an El Nino year. In fact, a 2024 study in Climate Dynamics showed that the number of Bay of Bengal depressions increased in El Nino years in the 1979-2020 period, averaging 3.9 during July-Aug versus 2.4 in normal years.This year there were 10 LPSs, including four depressions in July-Aug, against a normal of less than nine.What generally changes in an El Nino year is the direction of the LPSs. "In El Nino years, there is subsidence of air over south India and its adjoining northern parts. This prevents formation of LPSs in the southern latitudes, say in central Bay of Bengal, which would normally move towards the north Andhra-south Odisha coast," said IMD director general Mrutyunjay Mohapatra.Here's where Delhi benefited, particularly in Aug, when as many as six LPSs, including two depressions, impacted India. With a northward shift, most of these systems entered inland over north Odisha-Bengal and tracked north-northwest, affecting Odisha, Bengal, Jharkhand, UP, Uttarakhand and the Delhi region, with lesser impact in Rajasthan, Haryana and Punjab.There was another factor in play, likely linked to climate change. WDs are moist wind systems moving east from the Mediterranean region that usually bring wet weather to north India in winter through early summer. Historically, WDs are rare during the monsoons as the jet stream, which causes the disturbance, typically migrates north of the Himalayas by April-May. However, in recent years, the jet stream has persistently been retreating late, a trend scientists attribute to global warming. This year, there were 16 WDs in the June-Aug period - eight in Aug alone, as per IMD.There were several instances of the easterly monsoon system interacting with a WD, intensifying rainfall over parts of north India, including Delhi. For instance, monsoon's onset over the capital on July 2 happened during an active WD spell. The heaviest rain spells in Delhi (July 8-9, July 29, Aug 7-8, Aug 25) occurred when both a monsoon system and a WD were simultaneously active in the region. These interactions also brought heavy rains in west UP and left a catastrophic footprint in the hills - the Bandipora (J&K) cloudburst, fatal flash floods in Chamba (HP) and forced closure of around 290 roads across HP and Uttarakhand - but don't appear to have majorly impacted Haryana and Punjab.
Article Summary: Delhi had a season’s rainfall surplus of 8% in a meteorological subdivision (haryana) just north of the capital lies a swathe of deficient districts starting with neighbouring sonipat. El nino as well as climate change may have played a role in giving the capital an unlikely monsoon bounty.

Article Title: CGHS 'family' expands, but contribution stays unchanged
Article Text:
On Sept 1, the eligibility criteria for CGHS was expanded to include married sons and brothers of scheme card holders who are critically or terminally ill

On Sept 7, the health ministry extended coverage of Central Govt Health Scheme (CGHS) to adopted sisters of scheme beneficiaries. On Sept 1, the eligibility criteria for CGHS was expanded to include married sons and brothers of scheme card holders who are critically or terminally ill. Over the years, the criteria for beneficiaries have been steadily expanded. Yet the contribution by the cardholder remains the same, unlike in health insurance where the addition of a beneficiary, especially an elderly or ill beneficiary, could entail a steep increase in the premium paid.According to the Sept 7 office memorandum, the ministry received references "regarding the eligibility of adopted sisters (i.e. sisters adopted by parents of a CGHS beneficiary) for inclusion as dependent family members under CGHS". The 'sisters' have to be legally adopted by the parents of CGHS beneficiary and have to satisfy the existing criteria of dependency (staying in the same house as the cardholder), income ceiling (not be earning more than Rs 9,000 per month plus the applicable dearness allowance) and marital status (i.e. be unmarried, divorced, abandoned or separated), as applicable to biological sisters.The coverage of sons and brothers of beneficiaries was earlier available only to unmarried dependents. There were also age limits of 25 for sons and 18 for brothers, except for those permanently disabled, who were covered for life. The office memorandum issued by the health ministry on Sept 1 spelt out that "marriage shall not constitute a ground for cessation of CHS/medical attendance facilities in respect of dependent son or brother covered under these provisions whether on account of critical/terminal illness or permanent disability. .."Also, the lifetime coverage would now also apply for "chronic, severe, critical or terminal illnesses resulting in substantial and continuing functional impairment or inability to earn a livelihood/self-sufficiency".The addition of critically terminally ill beneficiaries could have a major financial implication for the exchequer as there is no ceiling on the amount spent on CGHS beneficiaries. Since no health insurance would normally cover a critically or terminally ill person, this expansion is fortuitous for an ill person, but only if s/he has a parent or sibling who is a CGHS cardholder.For dependent daughters and sisters there has never been any age limit but the coverage stops once they get married or get a job with salary above the stipulated limit. Similarly, unmarried/divorced/abandoned/separated daughters and sisters have been eligible for coverage for life, provided they fulfilled the condition of dependency and income. Children and siblings are required to "normally reside" with the primary cardholder to qualify for benefits.
Article Summary: On sept 7, the health ministry extended coverage of central govt health scheme to adopted sisters of scheme beneficiaries. The coverage of sons and brothers of beneficiaries was earlier available only to unmarried dependents. The addition of critically terminally ill beneficiaries could have a major financial implication for the exchequer.

Article Title: CBI mounts probe into US body's funding network
Article Text:
FIR Slapped On Missionary Org

NEW DELHI: CBI has filed an FIR and launched a probe into an illegal funding network operated by US-based Christian missionary organisation, The Timothy Initiative, and its Indian leadership for allegedly using foreign funds to the tune of over 92 crore between Nov 2025 to April 2026 for missionary activities in violation of Foreign Contribution Regulation Act The agency's probe has also revealed that the cash withdrawals were deployed across India to conduct training programmes, preaching, and the targeted indoctrination of economically marginalised groups, which,CBI said, fostered left-wing extremism.CBI kicked off the probe following directions and approval from MHA. Key individuals named in the conspiracy include India operations head Jonathan S Rajan, primary financial handler Micah Mark, Ajit Verghese Mathai, along with field operatives Varghese Chacko, Bablu Kurmi, and Supreme Joy.CBI alleged the syndicate conspired to systematically channel foreign funds into India without oversight.The FIR, registered on the basis of findings shared by ED, says that the syndicate circumvented formal banking channels by distributing over 1,000 foreign debit cards issued by the US-based Truist Bank across India. Operatives systematically withdrew physical cash from ATMs in states such as Karnataka, Chhattisgarh, and Assam.Investigators estimate that between Nov 2025 and April 2026 alone, the network illegally funnelled $9,995,240 into the country. This came in addition to an earlier illicit withdrawal of Rs 44 crore executed through identical ATM transactions between Jan 2024 and March 2026.The trail unravelled after agencies intercepted Micah Mark at Bengaluru airport on April 18, 2026. Mark was caught carrying 24 Truist Bank debit cards, all fraudulently embossed with the single alias "Santosh Kumar.""This was allegedly orchestrated on the instructions of Ajit Verghese Mathai to bypass Know Your Customer mandates and conceal the identity of the real users. Investigations revealed Mark had made multiple overseas trips to bring back such debit cards. Following the raids, TTI USA attempted to tamper with evidence by blocking domestic access to its website (ttiglobal.org) and remotely wiping cloud servers with data stored on seized laptops," the FIR says.This amounted to destruction of evidence as it happened even as search and seizure proceedings were underway, officials said.Rajan managed training logistics, trainer selection, and venue identification while submitting financial requirements to the organisation's finance team to secure illegal overseas transfers. Field functionaries handled cash distribution after making regular ATM withdrawals.The I-T department carried out searches and seizures on the outfit earlier this year.
Article Summary: Fir slapped on missionary org for allegedly using foreign funds to the tune of over 92 crore for missionary activities in violation of foreign contribution regulation act. Cash withdrawals were deployed across india to conduct training programmes, preaching, and the targeted indoctrination of economically marginalised groups.

NEW DELHI: In an important clarification on the ban on use of video clips of court proceedings, Supreme Court on Wednesday said if such footage was uploaded on social media, an aggrieved person could approach the authorities under the Information and Technology Act to seek a "takedown" order of the content.This clarification came from a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana while hearing a petition filed by an advocate whose arguments on July 1 before one of the SC benches on behalf of his father, accused of jumping bail, went viral on social media.Counsel for the advocate said unauthorised circulation of the proceedings on social media platforms had violated his right to life, liberty, dignity and privacy. "Continuous availability of the impugned videos on social media platforms, even after express judicial orders prohibiting such dissemination, constitutes an ongoing and irreparable injury to the petitioner's fundamental rights," he said.The bench said the SC had passed the ban order on July 24, and the lawyer could approach authorities under the IT Act and seek takedown orders against digital and social media platforms for deleting the alleged offensive content being circulated despite a ban imposed by the top court.CJI Kant said there was an efficacious remedy available to the advocate and he must avail that. However, he clarified that if any social media or digital platform used footage from livestreaming of court proceedings and either added a narrative or exhibited clips selectively to convey a different meaning, it would be viewed very seriously and may amount to contempt of court."If someone adds something to what the court observed or presents the proceedings in such a manner to generate controversy, we will take a very serious view of such acts," the CJI said.The bench advised the lawyer to move the authorities under Section 69A of the IT Act or directly send a legal notice to digital and social media platforms to take down the offensive content. If the intermediaries or authorities did not respond to the request and the grievance remained unresolved, he could file a petition in the SC, it said.Frowning upon edited clips of live-streamed judicial proceedings accompanied by biased commentary flooding social media, the SC on July 24 had banned uploading, sharing and circulation of audiovisual excerpts of court hearings on social media and digital platforms and said any online posting of such clips would require mandatory prior approval from the SC or jurisdictional HCs.
Article Summary: Sc had earlier banned uploads without approval from sc or hcs sc had earlier banned uploads without approval from sc or hcs. Supreme court on wednesday said if such footage was uploaded on social media, an aggrieved person could approach the authorities under the information and technology act to seek a "takedown" order of the content.

Article Title: Don’t trust Centre unless it’s a written deal, J&K CM Omar Abdullah tells Ladakhi delegation
Article Text:

SRINAGAR: J&K CM Omar Abdullah Wednesday said Ladakhi representatives, who have been in talks with a sub-committee of the ministry of home affairs (MHA) over their demands for the region, should not trust the Centre on any assurance until it is in writing.“Ladakh has its own issues and we have our own problems. As a friend and an elder brother, I can give Ladakhi leaders one advice: please do not believe in any promises of the central government until they give it writing and sign it,” he said, adding that J&K fell victim to assurances that the statehood would be restored, which wasn’t.“We were also given a verbal promise that they would restore statehood immediately after the elections. It’s been almost two years now and that promise is nowhere,” Omar told reporters in Pulwama.On Sept 9, the MHA panel held latest round of talks with the Ladakhi delegation comprising representatives of Leh Apex Body (LAB) and Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA) in New Delhi. A day after the meeting, the Ladakh administration said that Centre has agreed to constitute a union territory-level elected body for Ladakh under Article 371 of the Constitution and that the Centre has sought the views of Ladakhi representatives on the proposed body’s powers and its relationship with the existing Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Councils.“The subcommittee meeting, first of all, discussed the formation of a UT-level body under Article 371 of the Constitution, as decided in the previous meeting held on July 3. It was decided that a UT-level body will be formed under Article 371,” Ladakh chief secretary Asish Kundra said.Ladakhi representatives from LAB and KDA have been in talks with MHA since 2023 for constitutional safeguards covering land, jobs, culture and environment.The MHA had formed a committee on Jan 2, 2023, led by junior minister Nityanand Rai, to address key issues of Ladakh. Since then, several rounds of talks have been held.

Article Title: At halfway mark of third term, PM Modi to hold 'Chintan Shivir'
Article Text:
The two-day Chintan Shivir is aimed at reviewing governance, improving coordination among ministries and shaping the government’s future agenda

NEW DELHI: PM Narendra Modi on Wednesday directed setting up of over half a dozen groups comprising ministers, each having eight members, to brainstorm on issues including self-improvement, communication and governance ahead of two-day “Chintan Shivir” of entire council of ministers scheduled next week, TOI has learnt.The retreat will be held at Seva Teerth and comes almost midway through the third term of Modi-led NDA govt. A similar Chintan Shivir was conducted on Oct 21, 2021, barely months after a major Cabinet reshuffle during the second term. At that time, deliberations focused on governance and policy making and this exercise was aimed at helping ministers better understand issues of governance. Different ministers had made detailed presentations with participation of their colleagues in the council.The next brainstorming session is expected to follow a similar format, with thematic discussions and presentations by different groups. This is being seen as taking stock of governance, improving coordination among ministries and preparing the govt’s future agenda.Officials said that recently ministries were asked to provide the actions taken on the recommendations of the 2021 Chintan Shivir meeting. Several directions were issued to ministers and ministries, including to have live dashboards of ministry’s activities, review progress and hold interactions with all staff to get feedback and ideas. “This was an indication that at any point of time there could be a review of progress across ministries,” said an official.Last week, the PM had asked all ministers to work on making official websites of ministries and departments more user-friendly.
Article Summary: The retreat will be held at seva teerth and comes almost midway through the third term of modi-led nda govt. A similar chintan shivir was conducted on oct 21, 2021, barely months after a major cabinet reshuffle during the second term.
